plan.contextUnderstands: Freelance translators working for agencies, when an agency has approved the invoice and the money has not arrived, trying to get paid in time to cover the month.

parts.title: A recent time
parts.subtitle: 4 questions · the idea is not shown

items.name: Prevalence
items.belief: Nearly all of these freelance translators working for agencies had this at least once in the last 3 months.

ask.summary: Keel will ask about the most recent time it happened, as a yes or no: This item IS the gate: "In the last 3 months, did [the circumstance] happen to you?" Yes / No. Explicit, never inferred from the story. No → graceful exit; the person still counts in the denominator. Yes → the story prompt (the anchor test), then the rest of Part 1. Never names the idea, the app or the mechanism.
ask.question: In the last 3 months, did you wait to be paid for an invoice an agency had approved?

items.name: Frequency
items.belief: Freelance translators working for agencies face this on 2 to 3 months out of 3.

ask.summary: Keel will ask about the most recent time it happened, as a count from 0 to 3: Count how many months out of 3 it happened on, not how many times it happened. Never shows the founder's range.
ask.question: On how many of those 3 months did you wait to be paid for an invoice an agency had approved?

items.name: Importance
items.belief: When an agency has approved the invoice and the money has not arrived, getting paid on time is one of the two difficulties freelance translators working for agencies would most like made easier, out of five.

ask.summary: Keel will ask about the most recent time it happened, as two of your five, the one they would most like made easier first: 'Thinking about that last invoice, which two of these would you most like made easier?' Your difficulty and the others you named, shuffled per study, yours never first. Never names the idea.
ask.question: Thinking about that last invoice, which two of these would you most like made easier?

items.name: Current solution
items.belief: For most freelance translators working for agencies, their way of getting an approved invoice paid falls short: it takes a lot of effort or lets errors through.

ask.summary: Keel will ask about the most recent time it happened, as your five outcomes, in order: 'Think of the last invoice. How well did' today's way, in your words, 'work?' Your five outcomes, in order. Never names the idea.
ask.question: Think of the last invoice. How well did your way of getting an approved invoice paid work?

items.name: Compatibility
items.belief: For most, on their last invoice, the agency could approve it on a platform.

ask.summary: Keel will ask about that same time, with the idea in mind, as one of four fixed answers about the one item you chose: 'On your last invoice,' the condition you picked, asked as a question: would you have been able to? Yes, easily · Yes, with some steps · Only with help or approval · No.
ask.question: On your last invoice, could the agency have approved your invoice on a payment platform?

items.name: Relative advantage
items.belief: For most, it would have made their last invoice better.

ask.summary: Keel will ask about that same time, with the idea in mind, as better, no difference or worse, and under better which of your advantages: 'On your last invoice, would' your idea, by its short name, 'have made things better, or not?' Those who say better tick which of your benefits would have been better.
ask.question: On your last invoice, would invoice payout service have made things better, or not?

items.name: Adoption friction
items.belief: Most would send each invoice through the platform.

ask.summary: Keel will ask about that same time, with the idea in mind, as one of four fixed answers about the one item you chose: The effort you picked, said to them, then 'Would you do that, or not?' Yes · Yes, if it was clearly worth it · Probably not · No.
ask.question: You'd send each invoice through the platform instead of by email. Would you do that, or not?

items.name: Existing sacrifice
items.belief: The problem already costs the payer about $100 to $300 a month.

ask.summary: Keel will ask about the last cycle, as what it cost them in all, one amount or a number of hours: One total, all code's: what it cost the team over last month when an agency has approved the invoice and the money has not arrived -- an amount or a number of the team's hours (priced at the project's rate by code, never shown). The decision-maker sees no context card and nothing of what the specialists said.
ask.question: Last month, what did it cost when an agency has approved the invoice and the money has not arrived?

items.name: Price
items.belief: The payer would think it worth $60 to $100 a month.

ask.summary: Keel will ask about the last thing they paid for to deal with it, as what it would be worth to them, on a fixed price ladder: The same item on the decision-maker's link: the anchor line names money and hours (hours are the team's time); the question and the bands are code's.
ask.question: What would a fix for late agency payments be worth to you a month?

items.name: Ability to pay
items.belief: Your price is 20% to 100% of what the problem costs them today: it could mostly be paid from what they already spend.

ask.summary: Keel will ask about the last thing they paid for to deal with it, as one pick: 'Think of the last tool your team paid for. Where did the money come from?' Four budget sources, easiest to hardest; its first sentence is the part's one anchor.
ask.question: Think of the last tool your team paid for. Where did the money come from?

items.name: Buyer and payer
items.belief: The agency decides, and nobody else has to agree.

ask.summary: Keel will ask about the last thing they paid for to deal with it, as one of four fixed answers about the one item you chose: For the last tool the team paid for: did the tested role have to agree before it went through; the fixed four.
ask.question: For that tool, did anyone else have to agree before it went through?

items.name: Purchase friction
items.belief: The agency owner's approval slows the purchase most.

ask.summary: Keel will ask about the last thing they paid for to deal with it, as one of three fixed answers about the step you chose: For the last tool the team paid for: did it need the tested step before it went through; the fixed three.
ask.question: For that tool, did it need the agency owner's approval before it went through?

items.name: Commitment
items.belief: Most are open to start a read-only trial now.

ask.summary: Keel will ask about the last cycle, as one of four fixed answers about the one item you chose: The same item on the decision-maker's link: if it were ready today, would you take the founder's step; the fixed four.
ask.question: If it were ready today, would you start a read-only trial, or not?

reveal.statement: When it approves a translator's invoice, the agency approves it on the platform, which pays the translator for a fee and gets back the money paid to the translator within seven days.
text: When it approves a translator's invoice, the agency approves it on the platform, which pays the translator for a fee; it gives the money paid to the translator within seven days.
